newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Rail basis offers stabilize.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Rail basis offers stabilize.

text.p: Soymeal basis offers in U.S. rail markets stabilized on Thursday following solid declines earlier this week, U.S. dealers said.
"I don't see many changes today," said one broker. "I think they finally slowed things down for at least a day."
Some offers in truck markets weakened, mostly in response to waning demand from livestock feeders, a dealer said.
"The meal market is still pretty sick," an Indiana dealer said. "The demand just doesn't seem to be there."
The dealer speculated compounders are letting inventories run low because meal is harder to store in hot weather.

Estimates for the National Oilseed Processor Association's weekly crush varied widely. Estimates fell in a range of 23.50 million to 24.50 million bushels. That figure compares with last week's crush of 24.386 million.
NOPA will release the crush at 0730 CDT on Friday.
Soymeal net export sales for the 1996/97 (Sep/Aug) crop year were a healthy 92,300 tonnes. New crop sales were 67,900 tonnes.
